question.text: Continuing the Kaveri Foods case: Ganga Growth Fund computed TV at end of Year 5 = INR 1,560 crore using WACC of 12%. What is the present value of this terminal value at t=0?

explanation.text: The Logic: PV of TV = TV / (1+WACC)^5 = 1560 / (1.12)^5 = 1560 / 1.76234 = INR 885.2 crore (approx INR 885.4 crore with precise factors). The PDF Step 4 of DCF uses the same PV factor for TV as for the last year's cash flow. The Trap: INR 1,392.8 uses only 1 year of discounting; INR 780 crore is roughly 1560/2 (ignoring the formula); the inflated crore option confuses units. Always discount TV over T years, where T is the last year of the discrete forecast. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C covers identical PV math. XXI-B uses same approach for listed DCFs. The choice of discounting TV at the 'end of T' vs 'mid-year T' is a common AIF valuation committee debate; IPEV allows either if consistently applied. Manager's Pro-Tip: Cat I/II DCFs often have TV contributing 60-80% of enterprise value. In your IC memo, disclose the TV% share — LP advisory committees look at this as a proxy for 'how much of value is in speculative out-years'.
